candidate_relations.reason: The immunohistochemistry (S100+, SOX10+, HMB45-, Melan A-, CD117-, DOG1-) and morphology (epithelioid and spindle cells, nested/fascicular patterns, clear cytoplasm) are characteristic of clear cell sarcoma, not GIST. GIST typically expresses CD117 and DOG1.

The clinical presentation (small bowel mass, melena), morphology (transmural infiltrative proliferation of epithelioid and spindle cells, nested/fascicular patterns, clear cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, mitotic activity), and immunohistochemistry (S100+, SOX10+, HMB45-, Melan A-, CD117-, DOG1-) are all highly characteristic of gastrointestinal clear cell sarcoma, matching the reference diagnosis.

The immunohistochemistry (S100+, SOX10+, HMB45-, Melan A-, CD117-, DOG1-) and morphology are characteristic of clear cell sarcoma, not GIST, even with schwannian differentiation. GIST with schwannian differentiation would still typically express CD117 and DOG1, which are negative here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: GIST with schwannian differentiation vs. clear cell sarcoma
